title: Ethereum FOMO grows as Bitcoin, XRP sentiment weakens – Why it matters
summary: Does bearish sentiment dominates Bitcoin, Ethereum and XRP as prolonged declines weigh on investor confidence?
content: Ethereum is experiencing growing FOMO among investors while sentiment surrounding Bitcoin and XRP weakens. Prolonged market declines are weighing heavily on overall investor confidence across the digital asset sector. Observers are closely watching how these shifting market moods might impact future price trends and trading activity for these major cryptocurrencies.
content_ta: Bitcoin மற்றும் XRP மீதான சந்தை ஆர்வம் குறைந்து வரும் வேளையில், Ethereum மீதான FOMO முதலீட்டாளர்கள் மத்தியில் அதிகரித்து வருகிறது. தொடர்ச்சியான விலை சரிவு காரணமாக முதலீட்டாளர்களின் நம்பிக்கை பாதிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. இந்த மாறுபட்ட சந்தை சூழ்நிலைகள் முன்னணி cryptocurrencies-களின் வர்த்தகத்தை எவ்வாறு பாதிக்கும் என்பதை சந்தை பார்வையாளர்கள் உன்னிப்பாக கவனித்து வருகின்றனர்.

title: Gartner warns $3.5 trillion in AI infrastructure spending faces write-down risk by 2030
summary:
AI infrastructure investments risk significant financial losses, prompting potential market consolidation and strategic reevaluation by 2030.
The post Gartner warns $3.5 trillion in AI infrastructure spending faces write-down risk by 2030 appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: Gartner has warned that a massive $3.5 trillion in AI infrastructure spending could face significant write-down risks by the year 2030. This financial risk highlights potential challenges for heavy technology investments, which may lead to market consolidation and a strategic reevaluation of future infrastructure projects within the sector.
content_ta: 2030-ம் ஆண்டுக்குள் AI உள்கட்டமைப்பு செலவினங்களில் 3.5 டிரில்லியன் டாலர் வரை மதிப்பு குறைப்பு அபாயத்தை எதிர்கொள்ளக்கூடும் என்று Gartner எச்சரித்துள்ளது. இந்த நிதி நெருக்கடியானது தொழில்நுட்ப முதலீடுகளில் பெரும் சவால்களை சுட்டிக்காட்டுவதுடன், சந்தை ஒருங்கிணைப்புக்கும் எதிர்கால உள்கட்டமைப்பு திட்டங்களின் மூலோபாய மறுமதிப்பீட்டுக்கும் வழிவகுக்கலாம்.

title: Firelight forces XRP-linked tokens lockup as withdrawal delay queue grows
summary:

Understand the crypto stories that matter and what to watch next. Get The Catalyst in your inbox
content: An activation on October 6 automatically locked existing FXRP stakes into a pooled cover backing system. This update pairs fee income with claim exposure while also introducing a longer withdrawal delay queue, impacting users looking to access their funds.
content_ta: அக்டோபர் 6-ஆம் தேதி நடைமுறைக்கு வந்த புதிய மாற்றத்தின் மூலம், தற்போதுள்ள FXRP பங்குகள் தானாகவே ஒரு குறிப்பிட்ட பாதுகாப்பு அமைப்புக்கு மாற்றப்பட்டன. இந்த புதுப்பிப்பு கட்டண வருவாயுடன் கோரிக்கை வெளிப்பாட்டை இணைப்பதுடன், நீண்ட கால வாபஸ் தாமத வரிசையையும் அறிமுகப்படுத்துகிறது.

title: Bitcoin eyes $87K as CPI data and USDT dominance shape November rally
summary: Rising liquidity and CPI volatility could shape Bitcoin’s November breakout as USDT faces resistance.
content: Bitcoin is eyeing the $87,000 milestone amid a November rally shaped by incoming CPI data and fluctuating USDT dominance. Analysts are closely watching rising market liquidity and macroeconomic indicators. These factors are expected to play a critical role in determining whether Bitcoin can achieve a sustained breakout while tether dominance faces key resistance levels during this period.
content_ta: வரவிருக்கும் CPI தரவுகள் மற்றும் USDT ஆதிக்கத்தின் அடிப்படையில் நவம்பர் மாத விலை உயர்வை நோக்கி Bitcoin நகர்ந்து வருகிறது. சந்தை பணப்புழக்கம் மற்றும் மேக்ரோ பொருளாதார குறியீடுகளை ஆய்வாளர்கள் தீவிரமாக கண்காணித்து வருகின்றனர். இந்த காலகட்டத்தில் USDT முக்கிய எதிர்ப்பை எதிர்கொள்ளும் அதேவேளையில், Bitcoin தனது எழுச்சியை தக்கவைக்க முடியுமா என்பதை இந்த காரணிகள் தீர்மானிக்கும்.

title: AI Debt Glut May Be Pushing Up US Government Borrowing Costs, BondCliQ CEO Says
summary:

content: According to BondCliQ CEO Chris White, a growing glut of artificial intelligence-related corporate bonds is trading wider in the market. content_ta: BondCliQ-ன் CEO Chris White கூற்றுப்படி, AI சார்ந்த கார்ப்பரேட் பாண்டுகளின் அதிகரிப்பு சந்தையில் பரவலாக வர்த்தகம் செய்யப்படுகிறது. இந்த AI கடன் பெருக்கம் US அரசின் கடன் வாங்கும் செலவுகளை உயர்த்தக்கூடும், மேலும் தொழில்நுட்ப நிறுவனங்கள் தங்கள் AI முயற்சிகளுக்கு தொடர்ந்து கடன் வாங்குவதால் பரந்த நிதிச் சந்தை தாக்கங்கள் பற்றிய புதிய கவலைகளை எழுப்புகிறது.

content: South Korea is planning a major cybersecurity overhaul for its financial sector following a series of attacks targeting banks and cryptocurrency firms. content_ta: வங்கிகள் மற்றும் crypto நிறுவனங்களை குறிவைத்து நடத்தப்பட்ட தாக்குதல்களுக்குப் பிறகு, South Korea தனது நிதித்துறையில் முக்கிய cybersecurity சீர்திருத்தங்களை திட்டமிட்டுள்ளது. சமீபத்திய ஆய்வில் 130 நிதி நிறுவனங்களில் பாதுகாப்பு குறைபாடுகள் கண்டறியப்பட்டதை அடுத்து, துறையை சிறப்பாக பாதுகாக்க கடுமையான cybersecurity மதிப்பீடுகளை அரசு பரிந்துரைத்துள்ளது.

title: Australia seeks feedback on crypto platform rules ahead of 2027 rollout

content: Australia is seeking feedback on proposed regulations for crypto platforms ahead of a planned 2027 rollout. The consultation follows Parliament passing digital asset legislation in April. content_ta: ஜூலை மாதத்திற்குப் பிறகு வால் ஸ்ட்ரீட்டின் மிக மோசமான சரிவின் போது Bitcoin மைனர்கள் 13% வரை சரிவைச் சந்தித்தனர். சூடான பணவீக்க அறிக்கை AI உள்கட்டமைப்பு மற்றும் கிரிப்டோ தொடர்பான பங்குகளை பாதித்ததால், TeraWulf, Core Scientific, Cipher Mining மற்றும் IREN ஆகிய நிறுவனங்கள் ஒவ்வொன்றும் 12% க்கும் அதிகமான இழப்பைச் சந்தித்தன.

title: Interledger Foundation Takes Its First Steps to Bring Instant Payments to Community Lenders
summary:
The Interledger Foundation (ILF) is working with five community development financial institutions (CDFIs) and fintech organizations to lay the groundwork for instant payments adoption across community lending, where most institutions still run on rails that take days to settle. Large financial institutions have leveraged instant payments for years, accessing and deploying funds faster. Community-based lenders, though, have lagged, held back by technical, regulatory and resource barriers. Through five projects, Interledger Foundation is mapping those barriers to develop a roadmap that gives CDFIs and the borrowers they serve access to the same infrastructure.
FedNow, the Federal Reserve's instant payment rail, lets financial institutions send and receive funds in seconds around the clock. While large banks have adopted it steadily, CDFIs, which have deployed $272 billion in cumulative financing to underserved communities, have been far slower to connect, with most still relying on infrastructure that settles in days rather than seconds. That gap means borrowers face loan disbursements that don't arrive when they need cash most and payment friction that pushes small businesses toward less favorable options. The regulatory environment is also shifting with the Federal Reserve's proposed skinny master account, a limited-access account that would include direct FedNow and Fedwire connectivity. If that eligibility broadens, it would give those institutions a direct route onto instant payment rails.
Against this backdrop, ILF is coordinating an initiative across five community-based financial institutions to map what blocks the sector from reaching instant payment infrastructure and what becomes possible when those blocks are removed. The five organizations include:
Village Micro Fund — Connecting cooperative finance to modern payment rails. Village Micro Fund is examining whether cooperative finance models, including investment clubs and community savings pools, can be connected to modern payment rails without requiring participants to interact with cryptocurrency. The organization is researching how its platform, EnDAO, which allows community groups to pool and manage money with shared governance, can integrate with ACH, wire transfers and FedNow.
Kiva — Understanding whether frictionless payments would serve the community. Kiva is examining whether frictionless payments would change outcomes for Native entrepreneurs and Tribal communities, rather than assuming they would. Working with Native entrepreneurs, Tribal partners and Native-serving organizations, Kiva is conducting listening sessions to understand the barriers to affordable capital those communities face before making any technology decisions.
Access to Capital for Entrepreneurs (ACE) — Examining the link between payment infrastructure and credit qualification. ACE is exploring how open payments infrastructure can feed real-time cash flow data into its borrower portal in Georgia, building more secure, bank-connected payment functionality into its loan approval and repayment experience. The longer-term goal is underwriting approaches built on borrowers' real-time cash flow rather than historical averages, shifting criteria and making capital more accessible to borrowers historically marginalized by financial institutions.
Washington Area Community Investment Fund (WACIF) — Mapping the repayment friction that instant payments could solve. WACIF is researching how entrepreneurs whose cash flow doesn't follow predictable monthly patterns experience the current loan repayment system, identifying where more flexible, real-time payment options could reduce the friction that pushes otherwise viable businesses toward default.
AltCap — Building a modernization roadmap for post-closing payments. AltCap is building a modernization roadmap for post-closing payments for underserved small business owners in the Kansas City region, combining direct borrower feedback with an assessment of real-time payment options to produce a concrete plan for infrastructure improvement.
These projects are the first domestic application of the work Interledger Foundation has done since focusing internationally for years. Interledger Foundation's work centers on building the connections that allow payment systems to talk to each other, regardless of bank or network. Historically, it has applied that expertise to community-based financial institutions in Uganda, rural community banks in Mexico and payment ecosystems across Africa. This initiative extends that work to domestic community lending, where the same principles that have connected institutions abroad can address the payments infrastructure gap that has kept CDFIs and their borrowers off the same rails that large financial institutions have used for years.
"Community-based lenders have long operated on payment infrastructure that was never designed with them in mind," said Chris Lawrence, Chief Program Officer at Interledger Foundation. "This initiative gives us the opportunity to understand precisely where those barriers are and ensure CDFIs are positioned to use the same instant payment rails that larger institutions have accessed for years, so the borrowers they serve can more seamlessly access financial services."
The findings from these five projects will feed directly into Interledger Foundation’s roadmap for community lender adoption of instant payment infrastructure, shaped by the borrowers and communities it is designed to serve. This cohort of organizations is only the first step in the organization's ongoing initiative to work with community-based financial institutions.

title: Chargebacks911 Taps Kount Founding CEO Brad Wiskirchen to Accelerate M&A and Global Expansion
summary:
Chargebacks911, the global leader in chargeback processing and dispute management technology, today announced the appointment of Brad Wiskirchen, Founding CEO of Kount, as Chief Commercial Officer (CCO) of Chargebacks911 and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of its financial institution-focused sister brand, Fi911.
The high-profile appointment signals an ambitious new chapter for Chargebacks911.  Wiskirchen will spearhead strategic M&A initiatives, pursue high-value partnerships and expand relationships with financial institutions, payment processors and payment orchestration providers worldwide.
His appointment builds on Chargebacks911’s established global infrastructure, extensive industry connectivity and expanding portfolio of AI-native technologies, creating new opportunities to accelerate scale, diversify capabilities and unlock growth across the payments ecosystem.
“Brad’s appointment is about more than expanding our leadership team.  It’s about accelerating what’s next,” said Monica Eaton, founder and CEO of Chargebacks911. “We’ve spent years building the technology, infrastructure and industry relationships that have positioned Chargebacks911 at the center of an increasingly important part of the payments ecosystem. The opportunities ahead extend well beyond traditional dispute management, and we're bringing together the talent, capabilities and strategic relationships to pursue them at scale.”
Wiskirchen brings more than two decades of experience building, scaling and commercializing financial technology businesses. As Founding CEO of Kount, he helped transform the company from a true startup into a globally recognized fraud prevention technology provider, culminating in its acquisition by Equifax and Wiskirchen’s appointment to General Manager of Equifax Digital Solutions. 
Wiskirchen also served as an industrial partner at CVC Capital Partners, a global private equity and investment firm, where he led the fintech investment efforts in North America.  Additionally, Wiskirchen was named Chairman of the Salt Lake City Branch of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, as well as a member of the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) Interdepartmental Working Group on Finance and Technology, High-Level Advisory Group. 
Wiskirchen has also served on numerous for-profit and non-profit boards in the payments, fraud, identity and compliance spaces, and he has co-founded and invested in many other businesses in those spaces.
"Brad has unmatched entrepreneurial acumen, understands the investment landscape and brings the commercial instincts and relationships to help us capitalize on opportunities that can meaningfully expand our reach,” said Benjamin Bridwell, President of Chargebacks911. “We're not simply looking to grow our existing business. We're looking to reshape what's possible across the payments ecosystem."
A key component of Wiskirchen’s mandate will be expanding the company’s presence across the financial institution sector as CEO of Fi911, Chargeback911’s dedicated sister brand serving issuing banks, acquiring banks and other financial services providers. Fi911 extends Chargebacks911’s core dispute management competencies into the financial institution market, providing tools for dispute processing, workflow automation, compliance monitoring, reconciliation and operational intelligence.
“What Monica and the team have built is remarkable, and I see enormous potential in what comes next. I haven’t seen a more impressive foundation of technology, industry connectivity and market reach,” said Wiskirchen. “I've spent my career building and scaling technology companies, and it's rare to find a business with this combination of proprietary technology, established market reach and opportunity for expansion. Chargebacks911 has already built the foundation. Now we have an opportunity to dramatically accelerate its scale through strategic acquisitions, new partnerships and expansion into adjacent markets. The convergence of AI, payments intelligence and financial services is creating extraordinary opportunities, and I believe Chargebacks911 is uniquely positioned to capitalize on them. I'm excited to work alongside Monica and the leadership team to help build the next chapter of this company's success.”
Wiskirchen’s contributions to technology and entrepreneurship have earned numerous accolades, including recognition as an Idaho Business Review ICON and an induction into Idaho’s Technology Hall of Fame in 2023.
“Brad brings the rare combination of entrepreneurial experience, investment perspective and deep industry relationships,” Eaton added, "We share a belief in challenging conventional thinking and building businesses that make a lasting impact. I couldn't be more excited about what we'll accomplish together - and it's an added bonus to welcome another fellow Idahoan to the team.”
The next generation of payments technology won't be defined by isolated solutions. It will be built by connecting intelligence, infrastructure and capabilities across the entire transaction lifecycle.

title: Continent 8 and FuturePath AI Launch Future8 Accountable AI for Regulated Industries
summary:
Continent 8 Technologies and FuturePath AI today launched Future8, an AI-native operating company built for regulated operators, formed as a joint venture between the two companies. 
Announced at SBC Summit Lisbon, Future8 combines FuturePath’s enterprise AI applications platform with Continent 8’s licensed global operating footprint, enabling the iGaming industry to deploy auditable AI without compromising compliance, data sovereignty and operational control. 
Built for highly regulated environments, Future8 enables operators to move from AI experimentation to production deployment by embedding governance, approvals and auditability into every workflow from day one. 
Continent 8 brings licensed data centers and a private global network spanning more than 100 locations, built over 28 years serving the biggest iGaming and online brands, along with AI-enabled Global Capability Centers in India, the Philippines and Bulgaria. The company also contributes operational expertise, jurisdictional knowledge and intelligence derived from one of the industry’s largest collections of regulated infrastructure and operational data, helping Future8 tailor AI solutions to the operational realities of the iGaming sector. 
FuturePath brings a production enterprise AI applications platform, with pre-built AI applications powered by coordinated agents, already running enterprise operations for Fortune 500 companies across multiple industries. Together, the companies are adapting proven enterprise AI to the workflows, controls and operating realities unique to iGaming. Unlike generic agent frameworks or toolkits, FuturePath delivers regulator-ready AI applications designed to solve real business challenges for licensed operators. 
Accountability First, Infrastructure Flexible 
Until now, the iGaming sector has faced a difficult dilemma: how to deploy AI at scale while maintaining the strict, policy-aware explainability that licensing bodies demand across every jurisdiction they operate in. Regulators have moved past asking only where data sits. They now ask how a decision was made, a question AI raises and infrastructure alone never did. 
Future8 is built to make that evidence automatic. Because its advantage is regulatory standing rather than physical location, it holds whether a workload runs in a Continent 8 facility, in a public cloud region, or in the operator’s own account. 
This allows organizations to standardize AI governance across jurisdictions while retaining flexibility in where and how workloads are deployed. 
“Everyone has AI. Almost nobody can run it in a regulated market,” said Mike Small, CEO of Continent 8 Technologies. “Future8 lets operators optimize their business and achieve efficiencies with AI that regulators can actually audit, in every jurisdiction they hold a license.” 
“Our AI applications – coordinated agents executing real business work – already run real operations inside Fortune 500 enterprises, with every action governed and auditable,” said Saurabh Bhatia, CEO of FuturePath AI. “Continent 8 brings 28 years of regulatory standing that no AI company can replicate. Together, we are building the AI application and accountability layer licensed industries will need to run AI in production.” 
Flexible Delivery, Any Stage of AI Maturity 

No two iGaming operators run the same way, which is why Future8 is built to deliver outcomes rather than tools alone. 
Future8 is designed to meet organizations wherever they are in their AI journey. They can engage through advisory services, managed AI-operated services or direct platform deployment, allowing them to adopt AI at a pace that matches their operational and regulatory requirements. 
Its services are organized into three offerings that meet operators at any stage of AI maturity, from first assessment to full deployment: 
AI Readiness Assessment for Regulated Industries. A structured evaluation of the operator’s estate, its automation opportunities, and the license conditions that govern them, concluding with a joint executive readout that maps where AI can be deployed and how it will be evidenced. 
Managed AI-Operated Services. Future8 assumes the operational workload through a global delivery network, staffed onshore, nearshore, or offshore according to what each jurisdiction requires, so coverage follows the license. The operator pays for outcomes, and the work automates down over time. As automation increases, operators benefit from improved efficiency and faster execution while maintaining the governance and controls regulators require. 
Platform Subscription. For organizations that prefer to run AI in their own environment, Future8 licenses the AI applications directly, layered with the jurisdictional policy, control, and evidence artifacts that make them acceptable to a regulator. 
The platform can be deployed within Continent 8 infrastructure, public cloud environments or customer-owned environments while maintaining consistent governance controls. 
Future8 builds on FuturePath’s field-tested enterprise AI, already proven in Fortune 500 environments, where AI applications, powered by autonomous agents, handle tens of thousands of complex workflows monthly and reduce resolution times by up to 40%. Forward Deployed Engineers work alongside operators to adapt and deploy it to their specific workflows, systems, and regulatory requirements. 
Across the iGaming industry’s business, Future8 spans IT and technical operations, cloud migration, finance and procurement, and player-facing operations, with every workflow governed, auditable, and evidenced to the regulator. 
Whether deployed as software, consumed as a managed service, or delivered through a hybrid model, Future8 combines AI technology, operational expertise and regulatory oversight into a single offering. 
Future8 launches with an initial focus on regulated iGaming, with a longer-term vision to support additional licensed industries where governance, auditability and compliance are essential to AI adoption.

title: TransUnion and Bankrate Expand Partnership to Power More Personalized Credit Offers for Millions of Consumers
summary:
TransUnion announced today that it is making it easier for millions of Americans to find personalized credit offers that meet their needs. The company's new innovation delivers smarter matching by combining Bankrate's lender marketplace with TransUnion's credit data and Monevo offers technology.
Building on more than a decade of collaboration with Bankrate, the capability gives consumers a more personalized experience and helps lenders and publishers reach consumers with more relevant offers. Consumers can access the offering today in TransUnion Credit Essentials, a free credit app and web experience that helps consumers take control of their financial health.
"Consumers have many credit choices and not enough clarity," said Steve Chaouki, President, U.S. Markets, TransUnion. "By combining TransUnion's data with our Monevo offers platform and Bankrate's lender partnerships, we've built a capability that makes offers more precise. Credit Essentials is our first proof point, and we'll bring this to many more experiences where consumers and lenders meet."
Bankrate's broad network of lender relationships and its marketplace and auction technology put lenders in real-time competition for consumers, so matches cover more products, more providers and more competitive offers. Monevo draws on multiple sources, including credit data, alternative data and consumer intent signals. Its decisioning engine then matches each consumer with highly personalized credit offers from a broad panel of lenders. Consumers see offers that can fit their needs, so they can choose with clarity and confidence.
Because partners can embed the capability through a seamless, low-lift technical integration, consumers can access personalized offers wherever they make financial decisions. It’s available today in Credit Essentials and can extend to publisher and affiliate sites, co-branded experiences for financial institutions and brands and AI assistants, where more consumers now start their search for credit.
TransUnion Credit Essentials Gaining Momentum
Millions of consumers have registered for Credit Essentials since its May 2025 launch, with membership growing approximately 50% in the last year alone. TransUnion's Q3 2026 Consumer Pulse study shows that more than half of Americans (53%) check their credit report at least monthly, and nearly all (93%) believe monitoring their credit report is important. Among consumers who check their credit report, one in 10 do so to learn which credit offers they may qualify to receive.
Credit Essentials gives consumers free daily access to their TransUnion credit report and score, real-time alerts about critical changes, credit education and personalized credit offers across credit cards, personal loans, mortgages, home equity, auto refinance, insurance and savings accounts, all in one place.
"Bankrate and TransUnion have helped consumers make smarter financial decisions for years," said Matt Fellowes, CEO, Bankrate. "TransUnion's data and identity insights, combined with Bankrate's lender relationships, auctions and marketplace, help consumers find the right products with confidence."
Credit Essentials is the first of many experiences the combined capability will power. TransUnion and Bankrate are exploring more product types to extend the offers to publishers, partners, lender platforms and AI-driven channels.
NoYesInfrastructure15 Oct, 2026
content: TransUnion and Bankrate have expanded their long-standing partnership to provide millions of consumers with more personalized credit offers. By combining Bankrate's lender marketplace with TransUnion's credit data and Monevo technology, the new capability delivers smarter matching and competitive offers. Consumers can access these personalized options through TransUnion Credit Essentials, with plans to extend the technology to other platforms and partners.
content_ta: TransUnion மற்றும் Bankrate நிறுவனங்கள் தங்களது நீண்ட கால கூட்டாண்மையை விரிவுபடுத்தியுள்ளன. இதன் மூலம் மில்லியன் கணக்கான நுகர்வோருக்கு மிகவும் தனிப்பயனாக்கப்பட்ட கடன் சலுகைகள் வழங்கப்பட உள்ளன. Bankrate-ன் சந்தை மற்றும் TransUnion-ன் கடன் தரவு ஆகியவற்றை இணைப்பதன் மூலம் வாடிக்கையாளர்களுக்கு பொருத்தமான கடன் சலுகைகள் எளிதாகக் கிடைக்கும். இந்த வசதியை TransUnion Credit Essentials செயலி மூலம் நுகர்வோர் பெற்றுக்கொள்ளலாம்.

content: Federal prosecutors in the United States have charged a California man with conspiracy to commit wire fraud. title: Solaris Adds Instant-Access Savings Account to ADAC Credit Card Range
summary:
The Berlin-based BaaS bank is rolling out a Tagesgeldkonto to ADAC cardholders, offering a 3.5% promotional rate for three months before reverting to
The post Solaris Adds Instant-Access Savings Account to ADAC Credit Card Range appeared first on The Fintech Times.
content: Berlin-based BaaS bank Solaris is expanding its offerings for the ADAC credit card range by introducing an instant-access savings account, known as a Tagesgeldkonto. Cardholders can benefit from a promotional interest rate of 3.5% for the first three months. After this introductory period, the rate will revert to a standard variable rate. This integration aims to enhance financial services for ADAC customers directly through their existing card management platform.
content_ta: Berlin-ஐ அடிப்படையாகக் கொண்ட BaaS வங்கியான Solaris, ADAC கிரெடிட் கார்டு வாடிக்கையாளர்களுக்காக ஒரு புதிய உடனடி அணுகல் சேமிப்புக் கணக்கை (Tagesgeldkonto) அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. இதன் மூலம் கார்டு வைத்திருப்பவர்கள் முதல் மூன்று மாதங்களுக்கு 3.5% விளம்பர வட்டி விகிதத்தைப் பெறலாம். இந்த அறிமுக காலத்திற்குப் பிறகு, வட்டி விகிதம் நிலையான மாறுபட்ட விகிதத்திற்கு மாற்றப்படும். இந்த புதிய சேவையானது ADAC வாடிக்கையாளர்களுக்கு மேம்பட்ட நிதி சேவைகளை வழங்குகிறது.

title: NBA coin scam returns – Suspected hack targets basketball fans
summary: Are memecoin scams still a major threat in 2026 after the NBA incident?
content: A suspected hack has targeted basketball fans as an NBA coin scam resurfaces. This incident raises ongoing concerns about the security of digital assets and whether memecoin scams remain a major threat in 2026. Authorities and security experts are urging fans and investors to remain vigilant against fraudulent cryptocurrency schemes exploiting popular sports brands and events.
content_ta: NBA coin scam மீண்டும் திரும்பியுள்ளதுடன், சந்தேகத்திற்கிடமான ஹேக் ஒன்று பாஸ்கெட்பால் ரசிகர்களை குறிவைத்துள்ளது. இந்தச் சம்பவம் டிஜிட்டல் சொத்துக்களின் பாதுகாப்பு குறித்தும், 2026-ம் ஆண்டிலும் memecoin scams ஒரு பெரிய அச்சுறுத்தலாகத் தொடர்கிறதா என்பது குறித்தும் தொடர்ச்சியான கவலைகளை எழுப்பியுள்ளது. பிரபலமான விளையாட்டு பிராண்டுகள் மற்றும் நிகழ்வுகளைப் பயன்படுத்திக் கொள்ளும் மோசடியான cryptocurrency திட்டங்களுக்கு எதிராக எச்சரிக்கையுடன் இருக்குமாறு அதிகாரிகளும் பாதுகாப்பு நிபுணர்களும் ரசிகர்களையும் முதலீட்டாளர்களையும் வலியுறுத்துகின்றனர்.

content_ta: ஹைபிரிட் டீசென்ட்ரலைஸ்டு கிரிப்டோகரன்சி எக்ஸ்சேஞ்சான EVEDEX, தனது $EVE யூட்டிலிட்டி டோக்கனுக்கான டோக்கனோமிக்ஸை வெளியிட்டுள்ளது. இந்த டோக்கன் 100 மில்லியன் நிலையான மொத்த சப்ளையைக் கொண்டுள்ளதுடன், பிளாட்ஃபார்ம் கவர்னன்ஸ், ஃபீஸ் பேமெண்ட்ஸ் மற்றும் ஸ்டேக்கிங் ஆகியவற்றிற்குப் பயன்படுத்தப்படும். மேலும், அதிகாரப்பூர்வ டோக்கன் உருவாக்கும் நிகழ்வுக்கு முன்பு புள்ளிகளைச் சேகரித்த ஆரம்பகால பயனர்களுக்கு வெகுமதி அளிக்கும் வகையில், சப்ளையில் 6% ரெட்ரோஆக்டிவ் ஏர்டிராப்பிற்காக ஒதுக்கப்பப்பட்டுள்ளது.

content_ta: TSMC CEO C.C. The post Ethereum dips below $2,400 as hot inflation fuels selling and long liquidations appeared first on CoinJournal.
content: Ethereum recently dropped below $2,400, falling over five percent in a 24-hour period. The decline followed stronger-than-expected United States inflation data, which unsettled broader crypto markets. Rising Treasury yields, a strengthening dollar, and increasing expectations for interest rate hikes added further selling pressure to ETH, as traders watched key support and resistance levels.

title: COINPAYMENTS and Motorsport Lab Partner to Bring Digital-Asset Payments to Supercars and Luxury Motorsport Travel
summary:
COINPAYMENTS, a global digital-asset payment infrastructure provider, and Motorsport Lab, an experiential motorsport company creating curated supercar journeys, corporate experiences and brand activations for private clients and global organizations, today announced a partnership bringing digital-asset payments to luxury motorsport and experiential travel.
Through the partnership, Motorsport Lab clients will be able to use digital assets to book select high-value experiences through COINPAYMENTS' integrated payment infrastructure, adding flexibility for an increasingly global client base.
The partnership comes as digital assets and stablecoins play an increasingly prominent role in global commerce. According to industry data, global stablecoin transaction value reached approximately $33 trillion in 2025[1], illustrating the scale of digital assets moving through the global economy.
For businesses serving international and high-value customers, digital-asset infrastructure can simplify cross-border transactions while giving clients greater payment flexibility. Through COINPAYMENTS, Motorsport Lab will be able to accept digital assets through an integrated solution designed for businesses operating across international markets.
Throughout 2027, COINPAYMENTS and Motorsport Lab will collaborate on curated motorsport experiences, client engagement opportunities and  international programs, connecting the digital-asset economy with the global community of supercar and motorsport enthusiasts. The first opportunity for Motorsport Lab clients to book experience with COINPAYMENTS will be the Master Control on Ice: The Ultimate Aston Martin Winter Ice Drive across Germany and Austria.
For over a decade, Motorsport Lab has built relationships across the global supercar and motorsport ecosystem, connecting clients with manufacturers, driving academies, racetracks, Formula 1, private automotive collections, automotive personalities and some of the world's most celebrated motorsport destinations.
Specifically, the company’s programs place guests inside the culture surrounding the cars: journeys through Italy’s Motor Valley, home to Ferrari, Lamborghini and Pagani; British motoring experiences connected to Goodwood and Aston Martin; classic Porsche and modern supercar driving through Barcelona and Catalonia; winter ice driving and drifting in Austria; and Japanese Domestic Market experiences from Tokyo to Hakone incorporating mountain driving, drifting, racetracks and Japan’s distinctive automotive culture.
The collaboration with COINPAYMENTS creates a bridge between these real-world experiences and the rapidly expanding digital-asset economy.
Stacy Belf, Head of Sales, North America at COINPAYMENTS , said: "Today's luxury consumer is increasingly global, entrepreneurial and comfortable holding wealth in digital assets."
"Motorsport Lab operates at the intersection of luxury travel, supercars, Formula 1 and experiential hospitality. Our partnership gives clients greater flexibility in how they transact while creating new opportunities for us to engage with this community through extraordinary real-world experiences."
For Motorsport Lab Founder Ray Chang, the partnership represents the continued evolution of a company he started around a single Ferrari 360 more than a decade ago.
"Our clients aren't simply looking to rent an exotic car or book another luxury vacation. They want access to the culture behind the cars: the factories, people, roads, racing and food, including opportunities to engage with and invest in technologies shaping how we drive, race and connect human and machine," said Ray Chang, Founder of Motorsport Lab.
“For our corporate clients, these experiences can also bring leadership teams together, reward and retain key people, deepen customer relationships, create differentiated content and open doors to new business. In many ways, it’s the next generation of the President’s Club, an alternative to the familiar golf trip or wellness retreat.”
"Whether we're taking guests through Motor Valley in Italy, driving classic Porsches through Catalonia, ice drifting in Austria or creating an experience around Formula 1, these are often significant international purchases. COINPAYMENTS gives our clients a seamless way to turn digital assets into unforgettable real-world experiences."

title: One in Three Younger Workers Fear AI Could Soon Do Their Job Better Than Them
summary:
One in three younger UK workers (33%) worry artificial intelligence could soon do their job better than they can, according to new research from European financial technology provider, payabl.
This compares with just 16% of workers aged 55 and over, revealing a generational divide in how employees view the impact of AI on their working lives. Across the workforce as a whole, more than one in four (26%) say they are worried AI will soon be able to do their job better than they can.
The findings highlight several central challenges facing businesses as AI adoption accelerates: how to use the technology while ensuring employees understand how it will change their roles and equipping them with the skills and confidence to work alongside it.
Jolita Strasunskaite, Group Chief People Officer at payabl., said: “AI is changing work incredibly quickly, and it's understandable that this creates uncertainty. What stands out from our research is that younger workers are among those expressing the greatest concern about what AI could mean for their role.
“Leaders shouldn't dismiss that anxiety, nor should we respond by pretending that jobs and skills won't change. Our responsibility is to give people clarity about how AI is being used, invest in the skills they will need and create an environment where employees see technology as something that can increase their capabilities rather than simply compete with them.
“The organisations that get this right won't necessarily be those that adopt AI fastest. They'll be the ones that bring their people with them.”
Putting people at the centre of AI in payments
The research comes as payabl. returns as Networking Sponsor of the European Women Payments Network (EWPN) Annual Conference 2026, taking place at AI House in Amsterdam on 3 November under the theme, Human-Centric AI and the Future of Payments & Financial Services. 
Merima Mahmutovic, Chair of the Executive Board, EWPN, said: “AI is already rapidly reshaping payments and financial services. This year’s conference is about ensuring that people remain at the centre of that transformation, from how AI is designed and governed to how it informs leadership, work and the customer experience. Bringing together different perspectives from across the industry is critical to that, and payabl.’s continued support helps us create the space for those conversations.”
Strasunskaite will join a roundtable titled ‘The Leadership Playbook for the AI Era’, discussing how leaders bring their people with them as AI transforms financial services. Christia Evagorou, Deputy Group CEO at payabl., will participate in the panel ‘Your Data, Their Model: Who Really Controls the AI Economy?’, exploring the ethics of data use in financial services.
Evagorou said: “Financial institutions hold enormous amounts of information about people's financial lives. As AI becomes more powerful, customers need meaningful transparency about how their information is being used and how it affects decisions made about them. Ultimately, there also needs to be human accountability.”
payabl.'s support for EWPN extends beyond the annual conference. Ugnė Buračienė, Group CEO of payabl., serves as EWPN Country Ambassador for Cyprus, supporting the network's community and mission locally. Strasunskaite will also serve as a judge for the 2026 EWPN Awards, taking place on 2 November ahead of the conference. The awards recognise individuals and organisations making an impact across payments, inclusion, education and community. Nominations are open until 20 October 2026. Submit a nomination for the EWPN Awards 2026.
Strasunskaite added: “Technology is going to change our industry enormously, but technology doesn't decide what kind of industry we build; people do. Who is represented when decisions are made will influence the technology we build, the risks we identify and ultimately who benefits from innovation.”

title: emerchantpay and LoopingOne Enable Digital Transactions for Motorhome Depot in the UK

We look forward to extending these capabilities to more businesses with complex, high-value transaction requirements.”

title: PPRO Partners with Damisa for Stablecoin-Powered Treasury and Cross-Border Settlement
summary:
Damisa, the regulated stablecoin-native settlement platform for cross-border business payments, today announced that PPRO, the local payments platform behind global payment service providers and merchants, has partnered with Damisa. What began as a focused deployment in the Latin American region is now scaling with PPRO’s global expansion.
Through the partnership, PPRO taps into Damisa's onramp and off-ramp network to move money. Damisa converts the funds into regulated stablecoins and moves them across borders the same day. The model replaces multi-bank correspondent chains with a single regulated rail, reducing the capital that has to be prefunded in each market and giving PPRO full visibility of every payment.
STARTING IN LATIN AMERICA
Latin America was the natural starting point. It is one of the fastest-growing regions for local payments, and one of the hardest for moving money out efficiently. By leveraging stablecoin rails, Damisa gives PPRO a faster and more predictable route to move its funds across Latin American markets.
Following the initial rollout, the partnership is now being extended to additional markets as PPRO grows its global footprint, with Damisa supporting collection, cross-border movement and local-currency settlement.
WHAT THEY SAID
“PPRO is one of the most respected names in local payments, having built their business on getting the local details right. We are proud to be the rail that makes their cross-border money movements faster and more efficient. Latin America was the proving ground: collect locally, move on stablecoin rails, settle in PPRO’s currency of choice the same day.”
Jordan Lawrence, CEO and Co-Founder, Damisa
“As we expand our platform globally, we continue to need fast and reliable ways to move funds across borders. Damisa gives us a regulated, stablecoin-powered solution that lets us settle in our currency of choice. The results in Latin America made the case for expanding it further.”
Almir Majcic, VP Treasury, PPRO
WHY STABLECOIN SETTLEMENT, AND WHY NOW?
Correspondent banking has been retreating from many of the corridors where cross-border demand is growing fastest, while regulation of stablecoins has matured through frameworks such as MiCA in the European Union and the GENIUS Act in the United States. Together, those shifts have made regulated stablecoin rails a credible settlement layer for institutional payment flows, not just for crypto-native businesses.
Damisa was built for that moment. It operates as a regulated, multi-jurisdiction platform, holding an Australian Financial Services License with AUSTRAC digital currency exchange and remittance registration, registration as a Money Services Business with FINTRAC in Canada, and a VASP registration in Poland, with Malta CASP and Payment Institution authorisation in progress. Sanctions, AML and transaction screening run on every payment. Damisa settled more than $70 million in the first half of 2026 across more than 90 countries and 70 currencies.

title: Spanish Banks Report 150% Spike in Fraud Conducted from Stolen Devices
summary:
Over the last 12 months, Spanish financial institutions have seen increases in attempted fraud sessions, attempted scam sessions, the average value of those fraud and scam attempts, and the number of digital banking sessions conducted from stolen devices. Stolen device fraud allows its perpetrators to profit twice: once by draining the victim’s bank account and a second time by selling the stolen device.
“In the first half of the year, our Spanish customers also reported a 35% increase in sessions involving malware,” BioCatch Director of Global Fraud Intelligence Thomas Peacock said. “That spike is consistent with the local increases we’ve seen in both job and investment scams, which often direct victims to install a bogus trading app or work portal that then infects the device with a piece of malware.”
Bad actors targeting the region increasingly impersonate legitimate institutions and the family members of their prospective victims, combining AI-generated voice cloning with live photo and video calls to build a convincing sense of legitimacy.
The Spanish banks reporting this data all work with BioCatch, which prevents fraud and scams by recognizing patterns in user behavior. Attempted fraud sessions at those banks increased by 19% over the last 12 months, attempted scam sessions by 46%, and the average value of a fraud attempt by 63%.
Other key report findings:
Scams most common fraud type: Social engineering scams accounted for 43% of all fraud and 60% of fraud losses in Spain over the last 12 months.
Bot sessions decline: As Spanish banks have improved their defenses against bots, fraudsters continue to pivot to social engineering attacks.
The report also includes a case study showing how behavioral intelligence identified a remote access attack on a corporate account.

title: Clearstream Appoints Philippe Mueller as Head of Digital Products and Transformation for Clearstream Fund Services
summary:
Mueller will lead the strategic development and market adoption of Clearstream's digital fund solutions, aimed at connecting traditional and digital financial markets. He will be responsible for advancing Clearstream Fund Services' digital product agenda across areas including digital fund distribution, distributed ledger technology (DLT)-enabled fund processing, transfer agency innovation and private markets automation. Working closely with asset managers, distributors, custodians and wealth management firms, his focus will be on delivering greater efficiency, connectivity and transparency across the investment fund ecosystem. Mueller succeeds Olivier Portenseigne, who is pursuing a new opportunity outside the organization.
Mueller brings over 25 years of experience across Clearstream and Deutsche Börse Group, covering fund operations, product management, market infrastructure, and large-scale digital transformation. Since 2022, he has served as Executive Director and Head of Transformation Office & Digital, spearheading enterprise-wide digitalization, delivery discipline, and the strategic integration of FundsDLT into Clearstream Fund Services. Previously, he held several senior leadership roles, including head of Issuer CSD Services, where he initiated next-generation digital issuance solutions, and Head of Investment Fund Operations & Client Onboarding. He has also served as Chairman of the Board of Directors of LuxCSD and as a Non-Executive Board Member of Origin Markets and the Luxembourg Capital Markets Association (LuxCMA).
Philippe Seyll, CEO of Clearstream Fund Services, commented: “Our focus is on helping clients navigate the evolution of traditional and digital fund operating models. Philippe's appointment reflects the strength of our succession planning and the depth of expertise within Clearstream. He combines extensive experience across fund services and market infrastructure with a deep understanding of our digital strategy, ensuring continuity and fresh perspectives.”
Philippe Mueller, Head of Digital Product, Clearstream Fund Services, added: “The investment fund landscape is undergoing a structural shift as DLT, tokenization, and digital workflows unlock unprecedented opportunities for efficiency and distribution. Clearstream’s distinctive strength lies in bridging these emerging technologies with established, institutional-grade market infrastructure. Bringing product development and transformation together allows us to execute with agility while supporting our clients at every stage of their digital journey. I look forward to working with our teams, clients, and industry partners to drive the future of fund processing and distribution.”

title: Akurateco Integrates with viaSocket to Automate Payment Operations Without Code
summary:
Akurateco, a white-label payment software vendor, has launched an integration with viaSocket, a no-code workflow automation platform that connects more than 2,300 business applications. The integration went live and lets teams run routine payment operations in Akurateco automatically, based on what happens in the other tools they use.
Five Akurateco actions are available in viaSocket: creating a checkout link, checking a transaction status by payment ID, capturing an authorized payment, refunding a payment in full or in part, and voiding a payment before settlement. Any of them can be added as a step in an automated workflow that starts in another app or runs on a schedule.
In practice, this replaces tasks that staff currently do by hand, switching between systems:
Checkout links: when a deal is marked as won in HubSpot or a new invoice row is added in Google Sheets, a checkout link is created in Akurateco and emailed to the customer automatically.
Refunds: when a support agent approves a refund in Zendesk, the refund is submitted in Akurateco, and the customer gets a confirmation.
Transaction checks: payment statuses are checked on a schedule and logged to Google Sheets, with a Slack alert sent when a payment is declined or stays pending.
Captures: when an order is marked as shipped in the merchant's order management system, such as Airtable or Salesforce, the authorized payment is captured in Akurateco without anyone opening the payment dashboard.
“Our clients spend time on steps that don’t require a decision, such as copying an order amount to create a payment link or looking up a transaction status for a support ticket,” said Andrew Riabchuk, Founder and CTO at Akurateco. “With viaSocket, those steps run automatically, and the team steps in only where a decision is needed.”
“We’re excited to partner with Akurateco to help businesses connect their payment infrastructure with the tools they use every day. With viaSocket’s AI-powered automation, businesses can connect Akurateco with their CRMs and other 2300+ applications to automate payment-related workflows, reduce manual work, and build more efficient processes with just a single prompt ”, said Divyansh Jain, Product and Growth at viaSocket.
How to get started
The integration is listed as “Akurateco” on the viaSocket marketplace. It is available to merchants whose payment provider runs on Akurateco’s platform, with no additional setup required on the provider’s side. The merchant requests three details from their provider: a merchant key, a password and an endpoint URL. They then sign up for a viaSocket account (a free plan is available), create a new workflow, select Akurateco as an action step and enter those details. No development work is required.

title: Acorns Acquires Frich, Expanding Its Financial Education Community
summary:
Acorns, the financial wellness company helping everyday Americans grow their money, today announced the acquisition of Frich, a community where young Americans learn about money from each other. Frich co-founders Katrin Kaurov and Aleksandra Medina join Acorns as Co-Leads of Education & Community.
The deal reflects Acorns’ broader goal of giving everyday Americans a real chance to grow their money. The acquisition brings Acorns a community of 1.6 million people and an organic creator network producing financial education content, extending the company's approach to reaching new investors through creator-led education.
Many people avoid investing because they feel like it's a club they don't belong to, and they assume everyone else understands it and they don't. That feeling often forms years before someone opens an investing app. This acquisition meets people in the peer conversations where they're already shaping their money habits. It also continues a pattern for Acorns: bring in strong fintech builders and let them build.
“Investing is intimidating,” said Noah Kerner, CEO of Acorns. “Doing it with others can help people get past that. Katrin and Aleksandra helped a lot of people say ‘I don't know’ out loud, and that's a good place to start. We keep betting on builders like them.”
Kaurov and Medina founded Frich in 2021 to address a gap in financial education for young adults. The company was built around the premise that people learn how to manage money from each other, through real, diverse stories from people like them, shared in group chats, comment sections and creator videos, rather than from spreadsheets or formal instruction. Along with its active community and organic creator network, Frich also developed a peer-benchmarking feature that lets members compare their financial habits with their peers’, answering a question many young Americans ask: is my situation typical?
“We spent five years getting people to talk openly about money,” said Katrin Kaurov, co-founder of Frich. “Acorns is the natural next step, because it lets us pair that conversation with investing and saving.”
“Money feels like culture when it's honest, relatable, and social,” added Aleksandra Medina, co-founder of Frich. "That's what we built at Frich. It's what we get to keep building at Acorns.”
Acorns has spent more than a decade building products for financial wellness across life stages, including offerings for kids, teens, young adults, and families. The Frich acquisition adds an entry point built on peer conversation, reaching people where they are already talking about money, often before they have decided to invest. It also gives Acorns a way to start reaching specific communities more deeply, through the conversations those groups are already having with each other. 
Existing Frich community members will be welcomed to Acorns. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed. Kaurov and Medina joined Acorns this month.

title: AI Rivals Human Advisers as Brits Seek Financial Help Without Judgement
summary:
Judgment, jargon, and embarrassment remain major barriers holding Brits back from taking control of their money, driving a shift towards AI assistants for money guidance.
When asked who they would feel most comfortable approaching with a financial question, 18% of Brits said an AI assistant, just marginally second to a traditional financial adviser (19%), as revealed in a study commissioned by smart money app Plum.
Social media, where ‘finfluencers’ are most prevalent, ranks lowest overall, with only 1% of respondents saying they would feel most comfortable turning to these platforms.

The study reveals that over half (53%) of Brits have avoided asking someone a question about money because they were worried it would make them sound financially inexperienced. The same percentage (53%) said they have pretended to understand a financial term or conversation, signalling a fear of appearing uninformed in front of others. 
In addition, more than two fifths (42%) said they would feel more confident asking questions on financial topics if they knew they were not going to be judged, with 38% saying anonymity would help. 
This lack of confidence is particularly acute when it comes to investing, with stocks and shares cited as the topics Brits feel least equipped to navigate (44%).
Commenting on the findings, Will Bryant, Director of Wealth Strategy at Plum, said: 
“It’s easy to see why people are using AI to manage their finances. Money can feel like a difficult topic, especially as there’s often a sense that you’re supposed to know all the answers. Being able to ask questions privately, without worrying about what someone else might think, removes some of those barriers. 
“But knowing which sources to trust is paramount to keeping your money safe. Mainstream LLMs are not designed specifically to help you with your personal finances and lack the context, data security and financial tools that you can find on a specially designed service like Plum Plan."
“Technology can be a powerful tool to help build financial confidence, but only when the right tools are used thoughtfully.”
Plum Plan is an AI-powered tool in the Plum app that can suggest financial plans and gives details on the best financial products based on customers’ goals. Plum then uses automations to deposit money into their chosen products, including ISAs, easy access accounts and more.
Plum Plan is designed by financial experts, so customers can be sure they are receiving the best possible information. Plum is aiming to offer Targeted Support, regulated by the FCA, in the near future.

title: Deutsche Bank Deploys Farsight On-Premise Across Investment Banking and Capital Markets in Europe and the Americas
summary:
Farsight, the platform helping global financial services firms become AI-native, today announced its partnership with Deutsche Bank. Deutsche Bank has deployed Farsight at present across Investment Banking & Capital Markets teams in Europe and North America, bringing specialized AI directly into critical banking workflows while keeping sensitive data, proprietary knowledge and workflow activity within the bank’s own technology environment.
The on-premise deployment enables Deutsche Bank teams to apply AI to internal data and workflows while maintaining greater control over how that information is accessed and used. Farsight can incorporate the bank’s prior work, internal standards and proprietary data into workflows tailored to how individual teams operate, including their preferred formats, processes and standards. Bankers can then generate and refine materials through an automated chat experience that incorporates context and feedback over time.
“Our teams have very specific standards for what goes in front of a client, and those standards vary from group to group,” said George Tierney, Managing Director, Global Chief Operating Officer for M&A at Deutsche Bank. “Farsight gives our teams a way to apply AI to their own workflows and materials while operating within Deutsche Bank’s technology environment. That combination of control and customization is critical to making AI work in a global, regulated enterprise like Deutsche Bank.”
Financial institutions are increasingly moving AI beyond standalone experimentation and general-purpose assistants to specialized workflows. For regulated firms, this shift depends on access to data, much of which is sensitive. Running Farsight within the bank's infrastructure allows the platform to put that data to work where it can have the greatest impact, while financial institutions maintain control over the data.
“Banks have spent decades building proprietary data, workflows and judgment that shape how their teams work,” said Samir Dutta, Co-Founder and CEO of Farsight. “Running Farsight within a bank’s own infrastructure allows that knowledge to remain inside the institution while becoming part of how teams use AI. By incorporating banker feedback, Farsight can help AI reflect how a bank approaches client work rather than relying solely on general-purpose outputs.”
The Deutsche Bank deployment builds on Farsight’s growing presence across financial services, with the platform supporting teams at some of the world’s largest financial institutions.

title: IMF and World Bank Group Release the ‘Bangkok Blueprint’ to Combat Cyber-Enabled Fraud in Digital Finance
summary:
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group (WBG) Managements today released the Bangkok Blueprint, a high-level framework developed in coordination with the Bank of Thailand that aims to help countries prevent, detect, and address the growing threat of cyber-enabled fraud in digital financial services.
Digital finance has expanded access, innovation, and efficiency, but it has also enabled fraud to occur at greater speed, scale, and sophistication. Cyber-enabled fraud is increasingly linked to transnational organized crime and is ranked by INTERPOL as among the most threatening crimes globally, alongside drug trafficking and money laundering.
“Cyber-enabled fraud has become a global challenge that no country or institution can tackle alone. The Bangkok Blueprint reflects our shared commitment to strengthen cooperation, build trust, and promote a safe and inclusive digital financial future for all,” said Vitai Ratanakorn Governor of the Bank of Thailand. 
Released during the 2026 IMF–WBG Annual Meetings in partnership with the Thai authorities, the Blueprint sets out 12 key considerations to help countries identify vulnerabilities and develop comprehensive, coordinated responses. By promoting a more coherent approach across sectors and jurisdictions, the Blueprint sees to strengthen trust in digital financial services and support their continued contribution to growth and inclusion.
“Trust is the foundation of every financial system. As digital finance expands, countries must work together to combat cyber-enabled fraud and preserve confidence in the technologies that support growth and inclusion,” said Kristalina Georgieva, the Managing Director of the IMF.
The Bangkok Blueprint is organized around five pillars: establishing strategic and legal foundations; strengthening the fraud-mitigation life cycle; leveraging existing risk-mitigation and enforcement frameworks; expanding domestic and cross-border cooperation; and promoting consumer protection and resilience.
“Digital financial services can be a powerful driver of economic opportunity, jobs, and financial inclusion in developing economies. Strengthening protection against fraud is essential to ensuring that people can use these services with confidence and fully benefit from the opportunities they create,” said Anshula Kant, Managing Director and World Bank Group Chief Financial Officer.
Recognizing that fraud schemes often involve social media, digital platforms, e-commerce, and telecommunications networks, the Blueprint emphasizes clear accountability and timely cooperation across the public and private sectors, both domestically and across borders. It encourages countries to tailor the 12 considerations to their legal, institutional, and market conditions.
“As digital finance becomes increasingly interconnected, our response to fraud must be equally connected. The Bangkok Blueprint provides a foundation for stronger cooperation and collective action to protect citizens and strengthen trust in the digital economy,” said Ekniti Nitithanprapas, Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister of Thailand.
By fostering a safer and more trusted financial ecosystem, the Blueprint seeks to help countries harness the full potential of digital finance to expand opportunity, inclusion and sustainable growth.

title: StraitsX Partners with Visa to Expand Its Reach to Over 100 Markets Globally Through Stablecoin-Backed Card Programs
summary:
StraitsX, the stablecoin-native settlement layer powering global finance, today announced that it is partnering with Visa, the world’s leader in digital payments to expand its card issuing capabilities globally to more than 100 markets. 
The milestone extends StraitsX’s card issuing infrastructure beyond its established footprint in Asia, enabling the company to support eligible card issuance programs globally and is subject to applicable regulatory, compliance and Visa requirements. This expanded capability is designed for fintechs, Digital Payment Token (DPT) service providers, wallets, and other businesses looking to build card programs that connect stablecoin balances and digital asset payment flows with Visa’s global acceptance network.
From rapid growth in Asia to global card issuing
The expansion follows a period of significant growth for StraitsX’s card issuing business in Asia. StraitsX reached an annualised card GTV of more than US$6 billion across its stablecoin-backed card programs.
With the partnership with Visa, StraitsX can now extend the infrastructure and experience behind this growth to businesses building card programs across global markets.
“Stablecoin-backed cards have become one of the clearest examples of how stablecoins can move beyond settlement and into everyday payments,” said Tianwei Liu, CEO and Co-Founder of StraitsX. “We have seen significant growth in this use case across Asia. Expanding our issuing capabilities globally allows us to bring the same infrastructure to businesses looking to build and scale card programs across markets.”

Connecting stablecoins with global card acceptance
Stablecoin-backed cards provide a practical bridge between digital value and existing payment networks, allowing businesses to extend the utility of stablecoins without requiring merchants or consumers to adopt an entirely new payment experience.
StraitsX enables fintechs, DPT service providers and wallets to build card programs where stablecoins can support the underlying funding and settlement flow, while cardholders continue to transact through familiar Visa credentials and its global acceptance network.
For businesses operating across multiple markets, this brings together stablecoin-native infrastructure and global card issuing capabilities through a single infrastructure partner.
This collaboration will also take into account the continuously evolving nature of money-laundering and terrorism financing typologies and ensure that such risks arising from this integration are properly mitigated.
“At Visa, we are focused on bringing the benefits of new payment technologies into the global financial system in a way that is secure, scalable and trusted,” said Rubail Birwadker, Global Head of Growth Products & Partnerships, Visa. Working closely with our partner, StraitsX, we are unlocking more ways to use stablecoins for real-world payment flows, while connecting them to the reach and reliability of Visa’s global network.”

Building global payment infrastructure on stablecoin rails
The expansion of StraitsX’s card issuing capabilities is part of a broader strategy to connect stablecoins with the financial and payment infrastructure businesses already use today.
Beyond card issuing, StraitsX provides stablecoin-native infrastructure for payments and settlement, enabling businesses to move and use digital value across markets. As new forms of commerce emerge, including payments initiated by AI agents, StraitsX is building the infrastructure to connect these new payment flows with existing financial networks.
By expanding its Visa card issuing capabilities globally, StraitsX is extending this infrastructure to businesses looking to launch and scale stablecoin-backed card programs across markets.

title: Nuvei Secures License to Offer Local Payment Acceptance in South Africa
summary:
Nuvei, the global fintech building the infrastructure for every payment, everywhere, today announced that it has secured authorization from the Payments Association of South Africa (PASA) to offer local merchant payment services in South Africa, expanding its ability to support global brands and local businesses through its global payments platform.
The authorization advances Nuvei's Every Payment Everywhere strategy, extending its presence within domestic payment ecosystems to help businesses optimize payment performance in every market they operate. By adding South Africa to its network, Nuvei is extending its local acquiring and payment acceptance infrastructure, transaction data, and operational controls to another major market, accessible through a single global platform.
Phil Fayer, Chair and CEO of Nuvei, said: ”Commerce is global, but payment performance is local. Our expansion into South Africa is another step towards giving businesses access to locally optimized payment capabilities at global scale. South Africa is one of Africa's most important digital commerce markets, and strengthening our presence here creates new opportunities for international businesses entering the region and South African companies expanding globally.”
A growing digital commerce market
South Africa’s B2C ecommerce market grew by an estimated 9.9% in 2025 to reach $8.48 billion, according to research published by PayNXT360. The market is forecast to expand at a compound annual growth rate of 8.3% through 2029, reaching approximately $11.66 billion. This continued growth is increasing the importance of locally optimized payment performance for businesses competing in the market.
Bringing global brands closer to the local market
Processing transactions domestically can improve authorization rates compared with cross-border acquiring, reduce processing costs, and give businesses more complete visibility into transaction performance. Direct access to local transaction data also supports more precise fraud management and enables businesses to identify and address sources of payment friction more effectively.
Global brands entering South Africa will be able to access these capabilities through the same Nuvei integration they use across other markets. Businesses already serving South African consumers cross-border will be able to establish a more locally optimized payments operation without adding a separate gateway, acquiring relationship, and reporting environment. That gives them room to adapt the checkout experience to local expectations while managing authorization, fraud prevention, reconciliation, and reporting through one platform.

title: Convera Appoints Four Senior Leaders to Accelerate Its Global Money Movement Platform
summary:
Convera, a global leader in commercial payments, today announced four senior leadership appointments: Mike Cahill as EVP and Chief Operating Officer; Jon Southall as SVP and Chief Technology Officer; Tui Allen as SVP and Chief Product Officer; and Chris Steinig as Chief Information Officer. Together, they bring extensive experience in building and scaling global payments, product, technology and operational platforms. They will lead the execution of Convera’s roadmap for an integrated global money movement platform that combines cross-border payments, FX risk management and multi-currency capabilities for businesses.
Convera’s strategy is built on a simple premise: as agentic commerce emerges and volatility persists, businesses operating across borders need integrated solutions. They need to send, receive and hold money in the currencies they trade in, manage FX exposure at the point of payment, and route transactions across the most appropriate payment rail for speed, cost and visibility.
“Businesses don’t just need faster or less expensive cross-border payments. They need to know where their money is, what it is worth and how to protect it as it moves,” said Patrick Gauthier, Group CEO at Convera. “That is the opportunity in front of Convera. Our global reach, FX expertise, regulatory depth and customer relationships enable us to solve that problem in a way few providers can. Mike, Jon, Tui and Chris are proven leaders with the experience, judgement and execution discipline to help us deliver for customers. Each brings a distinct perspective, and together they give us the leadership depth to advance our roadmap for integrated cross-border money movement.”
Advancing customer-led execution
Mike Cahill has been appointed EVP and Chief Operating Officer, leading Convera’s combined Product, Technology and Operations organization. Since joining Convera in June 2026 as Interim Chief Product and Technology Officer, he has focused on bringing these functions together to deliver a more connected customer experience. Cahill has scaled mission-critical financial platforms and led complex transformations at Early Warning Services, the company behind Zelle, as well as at PayPal, Boku and American Express.
Jon Southall joins as SVP and Chief Technology Officer from PayPal, where he managed the Large Enterprise Platform, which supports more than $1.5 trillion in annual transaction volume. He has also built scaled payment platforms at Boku and Braintree. His experience in high-volume infrastructure will help Convera deliver faster, more reliable and more visible money movement for customers.
Tui Allen joins as SVP and Chief Product Officer from Ticketmaster/Live Nation, where she helped modernize product experiences at scale. She previously built new solutions at Shopify. Allen brings experience translating complex customer needs into scalable products that are easier to use, integrate and adopt.
Chris Steinig has been appointed Chief Information Officer after leading Convera’s technology operations. A 25-year veteran of the company, he brings deep knowledge of Convera’s systems, infrastructure and operating environment. Steinig will connect platform modernization, enterprise technology and operational resilience to help ensure the company delivers its roadmap with the reliability and control customers expect.

title: Starling Becomes First Bank to Train AI Model on UK Sovereign Cloud
summary:
Starling is building a transactional foundation model (TFM) with support from NVIDIA that will be the first banking model to be trained and hosted within a UK sovereign cloud.* Working with UK cloud provider Civo, Starling is supercharging its ability to design tools for customers while also supporting the growth of UK cloud capability.
The model will be trained on proprietary Starling data from over 15 billion anonymised transactions to give the bank deeper insight into the needs and behaviours of its customers. In time, it will form a single intelligence layer - ‘Starling Intelligence’ - that elevates the bank’s AI capabilities and enables it to build entirely new experiences.
“We’ve made huge strides with our proprietary AI tools, launching the UK’s first agentic AI financial assistant and rolling out new features every week. Now we want to connect these tools with a single intelligence layer that’s trained entirely on the specific needs of our customers,” said Harriet Rees, Group CIO at Starling and a UK Government AI Champion for Financial Services. “We also want to take a leadership role in the development of home-grown cloud infrastructure, which is essential to European companies’ ability to diversify their suppliers and reduce concentration risk.” 
By training its TFM on Civo’s UK cloud, Starling is following recommendations made in the UK Government’s Financial Services AI Adoption Plan, co-authored by Harriet Rees and published in July 2026. The plan flags a reliance on a small number of global AI and cloud providers and recommends that government and industry broaden their partnerships to improve optionality and systemic resilience.
“AI will only deliver lasting value for the UK economy if it’s built on secure, resilient, sovereign infrastructure,” said Mark Boost, CEO of Civo. “Starling is leading the financial sector by training and hosting its Transactional Foundation Model on a homegrown cloud. Pairing NVIDIA compute with Civo’s UK sovereign cloud shows that banks don’t have to trade performance or innovation for control of their data, or depend on a handful of global providers.”
The TFM will be developed with NVIDIA’s financial services team, using NVIDIA’s Transaction Foundation Model developer blueprint, including NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries for GPU-accelerated data processing and NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel for model training. 
Optimised for high-performance AI workloads, Civo’s sovereign infrastructure, from NVIDIA Hopper GPUs to upcoming Vera Rubin deployments, provides the low-latency compute and advanced liquid cooling essential for real-time reasoning, autonomous systems, and agentic AI. It will create a reusable intelligence layer capable of identifying patterns in anonymised transaction data and supporting multiple applications.
“Banks are at the forefront of turning massive amounts of data into timely, personalised insights while also protecting customers from fraud,” said Aser Blanco, Global Head of Banking at NVIDIA. “By combining NVIDIA’s accelerated computing and software for data processing and model training with Civo’s UK sovereign cloud, Starling can deliver exceptional customer experiences while maintaining control of its customers’ data.”
Starling intends to put its TFM into production in early 2027, initially to improve existing AI services around fraud detection and then to augment Starling Assistant, the UK’s first agentic AI financial assistant. The Starling Intelligence layer will enable Starling Assistant to provide more personalised experiences, such as proactively serving bespoke budgeting guidance.

title: Plasma partners with Stripe to build multi-currency stablecoin cards
summary:
Stripe and Plasma today announced a  collaboration to launch multi-currency stablecoin cards, making it easier for people and businesses to spend across currencies and markets.
Built in close partnership with Plasma as a design partner, the aim is to make everyday spending simpler. Cardholders will be able to use the currencies they already hold, reduce unnecessary conversions and FX costs, and spend abroad as easily as they spend at home.
Plasma is building the financial account for people whose lives span countries, assets and businesses, starting with everyday spending. As a design partner, Plasma will work with Stripe to shape a multi-currency card experience around how these customers manage and use their money across borders. 
“We’re building Plasma for people whose lives and finances span countries. Partnering with Stripe gives us the opportunity to develop multi-currency cards around how those people actually live and spend, with a simple ambition: spend like a local, anywhere.”- Paul Faecks, CEO of Plasma
“Stablecoins make it possible to hold and move money globally. We're working with Plasma to bring that same flexibility to spending, giving businesses the infrastructure to offer cards across currencies and markets without having to build it themselves.” - Henri Stern, Head of Stripe Crypto and Cofounder & CEO of Privy
Stripe is expanding its stablecoin card infrastructure to support more currencies and stablecoins, giving businesses greater flexibility to build card products for customers operating across markets. The expanded capabilities will support:
Fiat currencies: USD, BRL, EUR, MXN, and COP
Stablecoins: OUSD and eligible GENIUS-ready stablecoins
Markets: Available in 30+ countries today, with plans to expand to 100+ countries in 2027
A cardholder holding euros, for example, will be able to spend directly in euros without converting through dollars first. Businesses operating across markets can issue cards denominated in currencies that match their spending needs, helping reduce unnecessary FX costs.
The launch marks the  first step toward a broader multi-currency experience. Stripe and Plasma are toward enabling cardholders to spend across multiple balances, with the appropriate currency selected automatically at the point of purchase.
The partnership brings Stripe’s fiat and crypto infrastructure and Plasma’s product together to develop a card experience around how people live and spend across countries.
With multi-currency support, people and businesses will be able to spend with stablecoin-backed cards across more currencies and markets.
NoYesPayments15 Oct, 2026
content: Plasma and Stripe have announced a partnership to launch multi-currency stablecoin cards designed to simplify cross-border spending and reduce foreign exchange costs for individuals and businesses.
